summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality evaluation results from the latest prompt tuning and a quantized model build. Discussed minor regressions on clinical note summarization edge cases, next actions include sharing prompt/spreadsheet, SE regression runs, customer to provide failing examples, and scheduling a small canary re-run.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can start — it's 3pm PT so we'll kick off. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Lena here.
[00:10] Tom Blake: Tom on my side.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Priya here.
[00:15] Jordan Kim: Great, Maya and Ethan from the SE team and Nina from CSM are on as well. Agenda is the weekly quality eval review, go over regressions from the latest tune, and agree next steps.
[00:30] Maya Patel: I'll share my screen in a sec, but quick context: we ran the prompt set v1.2 against the quantized-v2 build overnight, scored with the customer rubric, and aggregated by intent buckets.
[00:45] Marcus Reed: Quick question about the rubric — is that the same one we signed off last week or any changes?
[00:52] Jordan Kim: same base rubric, we added one extra severity flag for clinical hallucinations after Priya's note. Not a full change but an annotation.
[01:10] Tom Blake: We noticed a handful of summaries that dropped key vitals and one example where patient age was swapped with a medication dose, which is odd.
[01:25] Maya Patel: yeah we flagged about 18 examples out of 1200 where precision dropped below threshold, mostly in long multi-section notes. Could be related to the quantization path or prompt context window.
[01:45] Lena Ortiz: Are those mostly from cardiology notes or spread across specialties?
[01:50] Maya Patel: spread, though cardiology and neuro had slightly higher rates — longer notes with multiple lists.
[02:10] Jordan Kim: quick clarification — when you say "quantized-v2" that's the int8 path you tested with per-channel calibration, right?
[02:18] Maya Patel: correct, it's our standard per-channel int8 with KV cache preserved. We saw a small latency improvement but a few edge regressions.
[02:35] Priya Singh: From a compliance perspective we need to make sure any regression that increases PII leakage or fabrications is triaged fast. What's the plan to isolate those?
[02:45] Ethan Ruiz: We're running a focused regression harness that flags hallucinations by comparing model outputs to ground-truth key-value pairs — e.g., vitals, meds. We'll surface highest-severity ones first.
[03:05] Tom Blake: I can add more ground-truth alignments from our internal dataset, that should help identify if it's templating vs model error.
[03:15] Maya Patel: that would help. Also we suspect prompts with enumerated lists are truncating core context because the prefix matching sometimes overweights earlier tokens in the prompt. We're testing two prompt variants: one that flattens lists, one that adds explicit anchors.
[03:35] Jordan Kim: Can you show one or two failing examples?
[03:40] Maya Patel: sure pulling up the spreadsheet, give me a sec — okay example A, original note: long multi-section note, expected summary includes vitals HR 86, BP 130/80. Model output replaced HR with 8 6? and missed systolic.
[04:05] Tom Blake: that's the age/dose swap I mentioned earlier; in our data the tokenization sometimes splits 86 into '8 6' in the transcript, wonder if there's a tokenization / whitespace handling bug.
[04:18] Maya Patel: could be transcription artifact too, sometimes our ingest converts pdf tables oddly.
[04:25] Lena Ortiz: We ingest a variety of EMR exports, so PDF-parsed notes are part of the noise. We can't change that easily.
[04:35] Priya Singh: For compliance, we need to record which pipeline stage introduced errors: ingestion vs model. If it's ingest, different remediation than model tuning.
[04:48] Jordan Kim: agreed. Action: Tom to flag 3 representative failing cases where you think it's ingest vs model by Friday.
[04:55] Tom Blake: yes can do.
[05:00] Maya Patel: we ran the scoring by intent bucket: 'summary', 'action items', 'med list' — med list had the highest precision drop. We're pushing a variant of prompt that anchors med list with explicit 'MEDICATIONS:' token and forces the model to look there. Early results show small gains.
[05:25] Marcus Reed: Any tradeoff on verbosity? We need concise summaries for the UI.
[05:30] Maya Patel: anchor prompt doesn't increase verbosity, it just clarifies where to look. But the flatten-list variant trimmed bullets which helped recall but sometimes removed critical qualifiers.
[05:45] Jordan Kim: On the scoring spreadsheet we saw overall accuracy stayed within 1.2% but med-list precision dropped 4.8% on quantized-v2 compared to float baseline. That's the main regression.
[06:05] Ethan Ruiz: For root cause we have three hypotheses: quantization numeric drift, prompt conditioning for lists, and ingestion tokenization noise. We'll run controlled ablations.
[06:20] Priya Singh: On guardrails — are we still enforcing the hard-block for hallucinated PHI? We can't surface generated identifiers to clinicians.
[06:28] Maya Patel: yes, guardrail remains: any generated PHI-like tokens trigger a block and send alert. That is unchanged. The regressions we're seeing aren't generating new PHI but rather misplacing existing values.
[06:45] Lena Ortiz: can we see an example of where a generated identifier appeared?
[06:50] Maya Patel: we had one case where a medication name resembled a name in another field, system concatenated — it's rare but we blocked output.
[07:05] Jordan Kim: OK good. For actionability let's go through the agreed next steps: Jordan share prompt set v1.3 and the scoring sheet, Maya run regression harness on quantized-v2 and upload logs, Tom supply failing cases.
[07:18] Tom Blake: noted.
[07:20] Marcus Reed: what's the timeline to get a canary up to validate changes in production-like traffic?
[07:26] Jordan Kim: propose 2026-08-20 for a 10% canary with rollback hooks and tracing turned on. Are there objections?
[07:35] Priya Singh: need to confirm retention window for logs and whether anything with PHI leaves their VPC — we'll need to ensure audit logs are retained in their KMS-backed bucket.
[07:48] Nina Zhao: we can set the retention and KMS policy for the pilot; Jordan and Nina will coordinate.
[07:55] Maya Patel: small note — we tested a float baseline here in our infra and the float baseline matched customer expectations better for med lists, so if quantized-v2 continues to show delta we'll try quantized-v2 with BF16 fallback for certain layers.
[08:18] Jordan Kim: good. Anything else on scoring methodology?
[08:22] Lena Ortiz: can you add an F1 per intent and an error-type column (missing, swapped, hallucinated) in the sheet? That will help prioritize fix order.
[08:31] Maya Patel: sure, we'll add error-type and severity.
[08:35] Tom Blake: one more ask: can we add the model logits or confidence scores per token to help triage?
[08:43] Ethan Ruiz: we can surface normalized confidence per span but full logits may be large and sensitive. We'll do per-span confidence for the failing examples.
[08:55] Priya Singh: that would be helpful. Also need to document any changes to the guardrail thresholds we test during canary.
[09:05] Jordan Kim: on the canary we'll start conservative: 10% traffic, immediate rollback on any new PHI generation, and 24/7 on-call for the window.
[09:15] Marcus Reed: how will we measure success for the canary?
[09:18] Jordan Kim: primary metrics: med-list precision within 2% of float baseline, no new PHI alerts, error rate on summaries < 1.5%. If thresholds not met we roll back.
[09:30] Lena Ortiz: sounds reasonable.
[09:35] Maya Patel: technical note — we also observed a small latency gain ~8% with quantized-v2. So there's a cost/latency tradeoff to present.
[09:45] Jordan Kim: yes we'll quantify cost savings vs quality delta so you can weigh options.
[09:52] Tom Blake: for the regression harness, can you include a split by specialty and by source type (pdf vs direct EMR export)? That will help isolate ingestion issues.
[09:59] Maya Patel: yes we'll add those dimensions.
[10:05] Jordan Kim: quick check — any legal/procurement blockers for the canary?
[10:09] Priya Singh: procurement is OK, compliance will need the retention docs and KMS configuration which we'll review offline. No blocker as long as KMS and audit are in place.
[10:20] Jordan Kim: perfect. Anything else from Pinecrest?
[10:24] Lena Ortiz: just want a clear timeline and owners which we've covered.
[10:28] Marcus Reed: one operational ask — if you can include a sample dashboard widget for med-list precision over time that'd help product.
[10:35] Nina Zhao: we'll add a draft dashboard and share in the drive.
[10:38] Jordan Kim: recap of next steps verbally: Jordan share prompt set and sheet by 8/13, Maya run regressions and upload logs by 8/18, Tom provide failing cases by 8/14, Priya confirm retention/KMS by 8/16, schedule canary 8/20. Anyone disagree?
[10:55] Tom Blake: all good.
[11:00] Priya Singh: all good.
[11:05] Jordan Kim: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread with links. Meeting adjourned.
[11:12] (end)
notes: Customer is willing to accept small latency gains if precision stays within threshold
Quantized-v2 shows ~8% latency improvement but med-list precision regression ~4.8%
Guardrails remain in place; any PHI generation triggers block and alert
Next steps focus on root cause triage (ingest vs quantization vs prompt) and a conservative 10% canary
